newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close firmer in defiance of Dow fall.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close firmer in defiance of Dow fall.

text.p: * Shares surprisingly firm given Dow fall, higher NZ dollar
* Market closed with weak tone
* Election still pushed into background
Price movements close
LAST CHG
330 +2 * NZSC cap index -12.24 at 4,468.96
283 nil * NZSE-10 cap index +2.90 at 1,129.12
365 +1 * Volume $52.2 million. Futures up 2 at 1,134
689 -2 * Other movers - +6, +8
The New Zealand share market closed stronger on Thursday in defiance of a fall in the Dow, an impending general election and a stronger New Zealand dollar.
However, dealers said the market ended on a soft note, particularly lead stock Telecom, and a further lead down by Wall Street overnight could see it soften on Friday.
The NZSE-40 capital index closed 4.65 ahead at 2,239.60 on good volume of $52.2 million, boosted by reports of a portfolio purchase.
"It was a mixed bag and it felt a bit weak at the close," said First New Zealand Capital broker Jim Patterson.
Fletcher Forests was one of the day's star performers, closing six cents ahead at $2.06. Brokers said the bond sensitive stock was responding to foreign interest rather than bond price moves.
Telecom ended two cents down at $6.89, but still three cents ahead of its U.S. close.
There was good demand for Fletcher Building, up four at $3.37 although sister stock Fletcher Energy fell three to $3.43.
Ceramco ended one cent up at $1.36 but reported after the market closed that it expected a $1.6 million half year loss and will only break even for the full year.
Ord Minnett broker John Rattray said the equities market, like other markets, continued "sailing into the election as though there is no storm in sight".
He said the election on October 12 had been a known factor for so long that institutions and others had positioned themselves for an uncertain outcome.
A new poll due on Friday morning in the National Business Review may give investors fresh information.
